originalTitle: Republicans reportedly fear datacenter backlash could cost them Ohio Senate seat – US politics live
summary: Jon Husted campaign reportedly concerned that rival Sherrod Brown successfully channelling outrage over energy-guzzling facilities
content: Clearly frustrated that his attempts to force Iran into submission through airstrikes have failed, Donald Trump announced on Wednesday that he intends to inflict “the MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY!” “This will be Economic Warfare and Isolation on an unprecedented scale”, the president posted on his social media platform, with the possible assistance of his close aide Natalie Harp. “ANY country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences”, the president’s statement added. “Oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies — It all needs to stop NOW. You know who you are. This will be an ECONOMIC D-DAY, and we need all of our Allies to stand with the United States of America to isolate, and defeat, the Iran threat.” “These maniacs are on the ropes”, the president insisted, before again repeating that the aim of his campaign was to force Iran to renounce nuclear weapons, which it did 11 years ago in the nuclear deal struck during the Obama administration that Trump scuttled during his first term. Amid signs that the Ohio Republican senator Jon Husted’s support for the AI datacenters Donald Trump touts at every opportunity could cost him his seat, and imperil the Republican majority in the Senate, the National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) has reportedly warned leading AI companies that they need to arrest the public backlash to the massive warehouses springing up across the state. Husted trailed his Democratic challenger, former senator Sherrod Brown, by eight percentage points in a recent poll for Fox News, and the Republican campaign arm suggested in a memo obtained by Axios and then the Washington Post that Brown is successfully channeling grassroots outrage over the noisy, energy-sucking centers. “More than any other thing in this race, data centers are the anchor hanging around Husted’s neck,” the NRSC wrote. “If he loses and data centers get the blame, politicians across the country will take notice – and they will not go near the next one.” “This has become a sleeper issue for the entire election cycle,” the campaign committee added. A recent ad from Brown’s campaign blames Husted for encouraging the rapid expansion of datacenters in Ohio. Charlie Blaettler, political director of the Guardrails Alliance, a Democratic Super PAC formed to combat “AI billionaire Trump donors trying to buy our elections and prevent common sense regulation”, said in a statement that the memo proves that the Republican party “is panicking because they sold out to the AI industry – a while ago – and they know it”. Republicans, Blaettler said, “are realizing how wildly unpopular Big AI’s agenda is with the American people. Now the GOP and AI’s unaccountable billionaires are scrambling to backtrack and find a new way to pull the wool over the eyes of the public so they can get what they want: A Congress that will do their bidding and an AI future that benefits them, not the many.” “It is time for the Democratic party to make it clear who they stand with”, he added. “A handful of Big Tech billionaires or the majority of people in the country who want commonsense regulation for this unprecedented technology.” When he was asked by a Maga influencer about the public unease with AI datacenters on Wednesday, Trump argued they generate tax revenue and construction jobs, “and many of them are designed in a very beautiful way”. The US debt reached $40tn for the first time on Wednesday, the US treasury department said, after the government deficit doubled over the last decade. The treasury’s latest debt balance showed $40.047tn on Tuesday afternoon, the highest in US history. The milestone marks years of government spending that grew under both Donald Trump and Joe Biden. During his first term, Trump approved $8.4tn worth of debt, with a huge chunk going to Covid-19 relief spending, while Biden approved $4.3tn worth of debt, according to the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget. In fiscal year 2026, which started in October 2026, $1.8tn has been added to the debt so far, with a big chunk of new government spending dedicated to tariff refunds, which have totaled $100bn so far, according to the Bipartisan Policy Center. Government spending watchdog groups have anticipated for weeks the US surpassing the $40tn threshold after debt reached $39tn in March. “For perspective, it took nearly 200 years for America’s gross debt to reach $1 trillion for the first time in 1981,” said Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget in a statement. “$40 trillion of debt doesn’t exist solely on the government’s ledgers; it is felt throughout the economy and finds its way to the pocketbooks of people one way or another. The more we borrow, the more we exacerbate inflation, squeeze out other priorities in the budget, and leave ourselves vulnerable to emergencies at home and turmoil abroad.” The threshold was breached as Congress, currently out of session, remains at an impasse over its latest spending bill. The US House and Senate passed two different bills that would fund the federal government, which is scheduled to shut down on 30 September if a bill isn’t adopted by both chambers and signed by the president. The president of Reproductive Freedom for All, the advocacy group for abortion rights formerly known as Naral, strongly condemned Donald Trump’s pick to be the new commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Dr Heidi Overton. The group’s president, Mini Timmaraju, strongly condemned Overton in this blistering statement: Donald Trump is trying to put an anti-abortion extremist in charge of any agency that could seriously undermine reproductive healthcare – including the agency that could roll back access to mifepristone nationwide. chineseSummary: 据报道，乔恩·赫斯特德(Jon Husted)竞选团队担心竞争对手谢罗德·布朗(Sherrod Brown)成功地表达了对高耗能设施的愤怒
chineseContent: 唐纳德·特朗普显然对通过空袭迫使伊朗屈服的尝试失败感到沮丧，他周三宣布，他打算实施“有史以来对任何国家采取的最具破坏性的经济行动！”总统在他的社交媒体平台上发帖称，“这将是规模空前的经济战争和孤立”，他的亲密助手娜塔莉·哈普可能会提供帮助。总统声明补充说：“任何允许其金融机构、企业、机场或政府实体向伊朗提供任何类型生命线的国家，本身都将面临巨大的经济后果。” “石油走私、互换额度、现金转移、交易所、船舶登记、幌子公司——这一切都需要立即停止。你知道你是谁。这将是一个经济诺曼底登陆日，我们需要我们所有的盟友与美国站在一起，孤立并击败伊朗威胁。”总统坚称，“这些疯子已经陷入困境”，然后再次重申，他的竞选活动的目的是迫使伊朗放弃核武器，11年前，伊朗在奥巴马政府期间达成的核协议中就做到了这一点，但特朗普在第一个任期内破坏了这一协议。有迹象表明，俄亥俄州共和党参议员乔恩·赫斯特德 (Jon Husted) 对唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 抓住一切机会宣扬的人工智能数据中心的支持可能会让他失去席位，并危及共和党在参议院的多数席位，据报道，全国共和党参议院委员会 (NRSC) 警告领先的人工智能公司，他们需要制止公众对全州涌现的大型仓库的强烈反对。在福克斯新闻最近的一项民意调查中，赫斯特德落后他的民主党挑战者、前参议员谢罗德·布朗八个百分点，共和党竞选部门在一份备忘录中表示
